title: Deployment access patterns and SIEM ingest playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures recommended IAM role layouts, RBAC v2 entitlements, audit-log schema requirements, evidence automation checkpoints, and SIEM export mappings for each deployment mode (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It is intended as an operational reference for engineers, SREs, and compliance reviewers who implement or validate access policies and logging ingestion.

High-level goals:
- Provide a repeatable, minimal-privilege role model that fits all deployment modes while allowing deterministic exceptions.
- Standardize audit log fields and event enrichment so SIEMs can reliably detect policy violations and provide evidence for audits.
- Define evidence automation checkpoints and retention expectations for customer and internal audits.
- Offer policy template snippets and rollout recommendations for RBAC v2 migration.

Quick summary of differences by deployment mode:
- Hosted API (SaaS): central control plane enforces tenant boundaries. Primary concerns: token scoping, multi-tenant isolation, operator access controls, SIEM ingest of both control-plane and proxied inference traces.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): shared infra within customer tenant tokens; operator and infra roles have narrower surface area. Primary concerns: capacity admin roles, cost/throughput telemetry, encrypted KV access controls.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network + optional air-gapped control plane; focus on delegated admin, offline evidence collection, HSM/KMS integration.

RBAC v2: entitlement-first model (conceptual):
- Instead of monolithic role blobs, RBAC v2 maps small "entitlements" to capabilities and composes them into roles. This improves auditability and least-privilege composition.
- Core entitlements (examples):
  - ent:inference:invoke (token-scoped, per-model)
  - ent:inference:stream (streaming access)
  - ent:model:push (ability to upload model blobs to model registry)
  - ent:model:promote (promote model to production serving)
  - ent:ops:scale (modify autoscaling / pool sizes)
  - ent:logs:view (view audit logs / exported events)
  - ent:siem:export-config (manage SIEM export connectors)
  - ent:keys:decrypt (use KMS keys)

Role composition examples (compose entitlements):
- role:tenant-admin (tenant-level operator for hosted/dedicated): [ent:inference:invoke, ent:inference:stream, ent:logs:view, ent:model:push]
- role:infra-operator (platform SRE): [ent:ops:scale, ent:logs:view, ent:siem:export-config]
- role:model-onboarder (ML engineer): [ent:model:push, ent:model:promote, ent:inference:invoke]
- role:security-auditor (read-only): [ent:logs:view, ent:siem:export-config] (no model push or invoke by default)

Mapping to environments (policy notes):
- Hosted: tenant-admin should be scoped to tenant_id and optionally to model_id. Platform infra-operator roles must be split so operators cannot perform tenant-scoped model promotions. Use time-bound elevation (just-in-time access via approval flow) for ent:keys:decrypt.
- Dedicated: tenant-admin mapping remains but consider an additional role: capacity-manager (manage reserved GPU pools) which is allowed ent:ops:scale but not ent:model:promote unless explicitly approved.
- Private: prefer delegated roles where customer-admins map to entitlements in their identity provider. Redwood operator roles should default to zero unless explicitly contracted.

Policy template snippets (pseudo-JSON, replace placeholders):
- Minimal tenant-invoke policy (Hosted):
  "policy": "allow",
  "principal": "user:<email>@example.com",
  "action": ["ent:inference:invoke","ent:inference:stream"],
  "resource": "tenant:<tenant_id>/model:<model_id>",
  "conditions": {"ip": "cidr:0.0.0.0/0", "time-bound": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z TO 2025-01-31T23:59:59Z"}

- Operator autoscale policy (Dedicated):
  "policy": "allow",
  "principal": "service:infra-ops@redwood",
  "action": ["ent:ops:scale"],
  "resource": "pool:<pool_id>",
  "conditions": {"require-approval": "true", "approval-ticket": "jira:INFRA-XXXX"}

- KMS decrypt policy (Private):
  "policy": "allow",
  "principal": "role:customer-admin:<customer_id>",
  "action": ["ent:keys:decrypt"],
  "resource": "kms:key:<customer_kms_key>",
  "conditions": {"hsm_user_presence": "true"}

Audit log schema (required fields for every emitted event):
- timestamp_iso: RFC3339 timestamp in UTC
- event_id: UUIDv4
- principal: canonical principal id (user:, service:, role:, sso:external-id)
- action: canonical action name (ent:... or internal:...)
- resource: canonical resource path (tenant:<id>/model:<id>/pool:<id>)
- outcome: allowed | denied | error
- request_id: correlation id from ingress proxy or SDK
- client_ip: optional; include when available (CIDR)
- region: region code where event originated (e.g., us-west1)
- env: hosted | dedicated | private
- raw_payload: base64-encoded raw event payload for evidence (optional, recommended)
- trace_context: W3C traceparent/trace state if present

Field enrichment rules (important for SIEM):
- Always include tenant_id where applicable. For hosted/dedicated, tenant_id is mandatory. For private, customer_id maps to tenant_id field.
- Normalize principal forms: convert federated SSO identities to sso:<provider>:<sub> to avoid fragmentation.
- Map model hashes and canonical model names into model_id and model_hash fields to detect suspicious promotions or rollbacks.

SIEM export mapping guidance (logstash/tempo/managed-splunk):
- Export format: JSON-lines with each event as a single JSON object matching audit log schema. Avoid multiline stack traces in the top-level message; include them in raw_payload.
- Required indexing fields: event_id, timestamp_iso, principal, action, outcome, tenant_id, env, region.
- Recommended enrichment pipeline:
  1) Ingest audit logs via secure forwarder (TLS + client cert) into ingest cluster.
  2) Run lightweight enrichment: add geoip for client_ip, decode trace_context, map principal to team via identity map.
  3) Apply detection rules: failed-authorization-rate > 5% in 5m, model-promotion-without-approval, operator-elevation-outside-windows.
  4) Forward to long-term storage with tag evidence:true and retention metadata.

Evidence automation checklist (for audits & incident reviews):
- On policy-change events (model promote, role grant, infra scale), auto-create an evidence bundle:
  - bundle metadata file (JSON) with event_id, timestamp, principal, summary, list of artifacts
  - include signed audit log entries around the event (t-2 mins / t+10 mins)
  - include model manifest and model hash if relevant
  - include approval tickets or emails (link to Jira)
  - pull relevant metrics (latency/cost snapshots) as CSV for context
  - sign bundle with service signing key and store in evidence-bucket://<path> with immutable retention policy

Automation components to implement (names are suggested):
- scripts/evidence-builder/main.py (runs on worker; triggered by event stream)
- infra/siem-forwarder/connector-config.yaml (standardized connector for hosted/dedicated/private)
- ops/just-in-time-access/orchestrator.yaml (request/approve flows)

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Do not log PII in plaintext. If PII appears in raw_payload, mark the bundle with redaction_needed:true and start redaction workflow.
- For private/on-prem customers where logs cannot leave VPC, provide a certified offline evidence bundle format and a verifier script that Redwood audit team can run locally with customer consent.
- Time sync is crucial: require NTP/Chrony drift < 5s across infra that emits audit logs. Noncompliant nodes should be flagged as degraded for audit purposes.
- Retention: default audit log retention is 1 year for hosted, configurable for dedicated (contract-driven), and customer-controlled for private. Evidence bundles for SOC/PCI audits must be retained according to contract (commonly 3–7 years).

Migration notes for RBAC v2 rollout (recommended staged approach):
1) Inventory current roles and map to entitlements. Use small scripts to extract role-to-permission tables from existing policies.
2) Deploy entitlements catalog service and allow read-only referencing in policies (no enforcement).
3) Start composing new roles for a subset of tenants (pilot) and run in parallel with legacy RBAC.
4) Implement enforcement toggles by tenant and enforce entitlements for API endpoints; monitor denials and reduce scope iteratively.
5) After 30–60 days of stable operation in pilot, expand rollout and deprecate legacy roles.

Appendix A — Example detection rules (SIEM queries, pseudo):
- Suspicious model promotion: events where action == "ent:model:promote" AND outcome == "allowed" AND approval_ticket IS NULL => ALERT high
- Operator elevation outside hours: principal starts_with("role:infra-ops") AND event_time hour NOT IN (0900-1800) AND env == "hosted" => ALERT medium
- High failed invokes: count(action == "ent:inference:invoke" AND outcome == "denied") over 5m > 100 => investigate potential attack or misconfiguration

Appendix B — Example evidence-bundle metadata (fields expected):
- bundle_id, created_by, created_at, related_event_ids, artifact_paths (list), retention_until, signature, redaction_needed

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: security-and-compliance@redwood.ai (pager: escalation channel #sec-oncall)
- Infra/SRE: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
- Product-privacy: privacy-lead@redwood.ai

Notes to implementers (short):
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive but must be adapted to contract-specific constraints for dedicated/private customers. Keep changes tracked in the linked GitHub PRs.
- For any deviation from the schema or evidence flow, add an entry in the change-log at confluence:SEC-Playbooks-814 and create a liaison task in Jira.
